[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CoreSite was founded in 2001 as CRG West, a Carlyle Group portfolio company, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. American Tower Corporation, the public tower and infrastructure company (NYSE: AMT, SEC CIK 1053507), completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. Stonepeak Partners LP later bought roughly 29 percent of American Towers US data center business directly in July 2022, increasing that stake to about 36 percent by October 2022. CoreSites own current Silicon Valley regional page (operator source, tier-1, https://www.coresite.com/data-center-locations/silicon-valley) names nine data centers on this Santa Clara campus, SV1 through SV9, totaling more than 1.4 million square feet campus wide, but only describes SV1, SV2, SV4, SV7, SV8, and SV9 individually, SV1 and SV2 are not rows in this registry. SV3, SV5, and SV6 are not detailed on that page, so their building specific facts below come from data center industry aggregator directories instead. CoreSites own regional page gives this specific building, SV4, an address of 2972 Stender Way, Santa Clara, CA 95054, with 101,000 plus square feet, this is corroborated by industry aggregators Baxtel and DataCenterMap, which independently list the same address, and by a CoreSite branded spec sheet PDF hosted on the operators own web asset domain. No MW or power capacity figure was found for this specific building in any source checked this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite SV4 is a 101,000 square foot building on the CoreSite Santa Clara campus in Silicon Valley, one of nine facilities across the site totaling more than 1.4 million square feet. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for this specific building, so its power capacity cannot be compared directly to other data centers or converted to an estimate of rack or accelerator count.

Among California's 103 mapped data center facilities, only 11 publish power capacity figures, and CoreSite SV4 is not among them. The state's published capacity totals 365 MW across those 11 facilities, placing SV4 at rank 12 in a list it cannot occupy without disclosed power specifications.

Without published power or IT load data, this building's relevance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from operator sources. Square footage alone does not reveal whether the space is allocated to colocation, to network transit, to older low-density infrastructure, or to the high-density compute clusters that drive AI training. The absence of a published megawatt figure, across both the operator's own pages and industry aggregators, places this facility outside the set of data center campuses currently visible to analysis of AI's power constraint.
